dimensions.assessment: Directly impacts members of the Advisory Committee on Reactor Safeguards, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission, and applicants for reactor licenses.
dimensions.evidence: The Committee shall consist of a maximum of 15 members, to be appointed by the Commission

dimensions.assessment: Modifies committee operating procedures, term limits, and the specific scope of topics the committee focuses on during license reviews.
dimensions.evidence: the Committee shall, to the extent practicable, focus on issues that directly relate to reactor design; are safety significant; are novel...

dimensions.assessment: Provides per diem compensation and travel expense reimbursements for committee members, but specifies no aggregate fiscal amounts.
dimensions.evidence: The members of the Committee shall receive-- (1) a per diem compensation for each day spent in meetings... and (2) compensation for necessary traveling

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Atomic Energy Act of 1954 to restructure advisory committee terms, license application reviews, and agency coordination policies.
dimensions.evidence: Section 29 of the Atomic Energy Act of 1954 (42 U.S.C. 2039) is amended

dimensions.assessment: Makes permanent structural and operational changes to the advisory committee framework within the Nuclear Regulatory Commission.
dimensions.evidence: Except as provided in paragraph (2), the Commission may appoint a member of the Committee for not more than 2 terms of 4 years each.

missing_information: Total expected expenditures for member per diems and travel expenses
importance_detail.rationale: Updates the structure, membership terms, focus areas, and review processes of the Nuclear Regulatory Commission's Advisory Committee on Reactor Safeguards.
